bibliographic.title: Robust blue-green urban flood risk management optimised with a genetic algorithm for multiple rainstorm return periods
bibliographic.authors: Asid Ur Rehman, Vassilis Glenis, Elizabeth Lewis, Chris Kilsby, Claire Walsh
bibliographic.citation_apa: Rehman, A. U., Glenis, V., Lewis, E., Kilsby, C., & Walsh, C. (unclear). Robust blue-green urban flood risk management optimised with a genetic algorithm for multiple rainstorm return periods. Journal of Flood Risk Management. https://doi.org/10.1111/jfr3.70118

methodology.method_family: multi-objective optimisation with NSGA-II genetic algorithm integrated with distributed hydrodynamic flood modelling (CityCAT)
methodology.study_design: computational simulation and optimisation study comparing single-return-period versus composite multi-return-period BGI designs
methodology.sample_description: urban catchment with 80 permeable surface intervention zones; rainfall return periods T = 10, 20, 30, 50, and 100 years; building-type damage functions for DDC and EAD
methodology.sector: urban flood risk management / civil and environmental engineering
methodology.technology_context: Blue-Green Infrastructure (BGI) spatial optimisation; NSGA-II; CityCAT hydrodynamic model; Depth-Duration-Frequency rainfall design; direct damage cost (DDC) and expected annual damage (EAD) objective functions

eligibility.exclusion_reason: The article addresses urban flood risk management and genetic-algorithm optimisation of blue-green infrastructure. The provided text contains no large language models, generative AI, conversational systems, chatbots, agents, RAG, or AI governance mechanisms relevant to the review scope.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Although automated triage matched generic terms such as risk, compliance, government, policy, standard, challenge, and question, these occur in a hydrological-engineering context (flood damage, rainfall standards, Scottish Government EAD equation, city planning policy). The study's core contribution is a multi-objective optimisation framework for BGI design across multiple rainstorm return periods, not governance of conversational or LLM-based systems in regulated settings.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Full text clearly establishes flood-engineering optimisation as the sole focus; absence of LLM, conversational AI, and AI governance content is unambiguous.

appraisal.notes: Within its own domain, the study presents a clear optimisation objective, detailed modelling workflow, and reported performance metrics (MedRD, MaxRD, AUPF). Appraisal is reported only for signals present in the supplied text and does not imply eligibility for the conversational-LLM governance review.

cerqual.explanation: The evidence is internally coherent for flood-risk optimisation, but it has very low relevance to conversational governance or LLM systems because the technology and governance objects are entirely different.

coding.theme: Urban flood risk management through multi-return-period BGI optimisation
coding.subtheme: Robustness of composite rainstorm-based design versus single maximum return period design

synthesis.main_claim: BGI schemes optimised for a single maximum return period perform poorly under other storm magnitudes, whereas a composite multi-return-period optimisation framework improves robustness and resilience metrics across return periods.
synthesis.contribution: Introduces a multi-objective optimisation framework combining NSGA-II with a distributed hydrodynamic model, using DDC and EAD as risk objectives across five return periods, with climate uplift stress testing.
synthesis.limitations: DDC reliability depends on accurate building classification; permeable surface zones may remain skewed toward higher return periods; trade-offs between spatial resolution and computational efficiency are noted.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude from central or supporting evidence for a systematic review on conversational governance in LLM-based regulated systems; at most incidental contextual value for generic risk-management vocabulary, which is not sufficient for inclusion.
